title: TSPO–PET binding in vivo reflects increased phagocytic microglia at post mortem in people with frontotemporal dementia
title_zh: TSPO–PET 体内结合反映前额颞叶痴呆患者尸检时吞噬性小胶质细胞增加
abstract: Abstract Brain inflammation is a key feature of frontotemporal dementia (FTD). Positron emission tomography (PET) of the 18 kDa translocator protein (TSPO) is widely used as an in vivo proxy for neuroinflammation, but whether the elevated signal reflects microglial, astrocytic or vascular pathology remains controversial, and this has not previously been resolved in FTD using matched ante mortem imaging and post-mortem tissue. We paired ante mortem [ 11 C]PK11195 TSPO–PET with quantitative post-mortem neuropathology in 10 individuals with FTD (5 FTLD-tau, 5 FTLD–TDP) and 5 age- and sex-matched controls, combining CD68 immunohistochemistry across 17 brain regions, multiplex immunofluorescence pairing TSPO with microglial/macrophagic (IBA1, CD68), astrocytic (GFAP) and endothelial (CD31) markers in three frontotemporal cortical regions, and three-dimensional single-cell reconstruction of individual microglia. CD68 area fraction was elevated in FTD relative to controls, predominantly in white matter, and was positively associated with regional TSPO–PET-binding potential across the cohort ( β = 8.66, P < 0.001), with comparable slopes in FTLD-tau and FTLD–TDP. Total tissue TSPO-area fraction was likewise increased in FTD and tracked regional PET binding in two independently processed slide sets. Of the four cell-type markers, only the CD68–TSPO co-localised fraction was positively associated with the PET signal ( β = +0.0041, P = 0.015, P FDR = 0.062), with null or negative associations for IBA1, GFAP and CD31. At single-cell resolution, IBA1+ microglia that were also CD68+ carried more absolute TSPO and were larger than CD68− microglia, without an increase in the TSPO fraction of cell volume. The elevated TSPO–PET signal in FTD, therefore, likely reflects an increased burden of CD68+ phagocytic microglia rather than TSPO expression in other cell types, supporting TSPO–PET as a microglial-burden biomarker across both FTLD-tau and FTLD–TDP.
abstract_zh: 摘要 脑炎症是前额颞叶痴呆（FTD）的关键特征。18 kDa 转位蛋白（TSPO）的正电子发射断层扫描（PET）被广泛用作神经炎症的体内代理，但升高的信号是否反映小胶质细胞、星形胶质细胞或血管病理仍有争议，且在使用匹配的活体成像和尸检组织之前尚未在 FTD 中得到解决。我们将活体 [11C]PK11195 TSPO–PET 与 10 名 FTD 患者（5 名 FTLD‑tau，5 名 FTLD‑TDP）和 5 名年龄性别匹配对照的定量尸检神经病理学相结合，使用 CD68 免疫组化在 17 个脑区进行分析，使用多重免疫荧光将 TSPO 与小胶质/巨噬细胞（IBA1、CD68）、星形胶质细胞（GFAP）和内皮细胞（CD31）标记在三个位于前额颞叶皮层的区域进行配对，并对单个小胶质细胞进行三维单细胞重建。CD68 区域占比在 FTD 中高于对照，主要集中在白质，并与整个队列的区域性 TSPO–PET 结合潜能呈正相关（β = 8.66，P < 0.001），FTLD‑tau 与 FTLD‑TDP 的斜率相似。总组织 TSPO 区域占比在 FTD 中亦升高，并在两套独立处理的切片中跟踪区域 PET 结合。四种细胞类型标记中，只有 CD68–TSPO 共定位比例与 PET 信号呈正相关（β = +0.0041，P = 0.015，P FDR = 0.062），而 IBA1、GFAP 和 CD31 则无或呈负相关。在单细胞分辨率下，IBA1+ 且 CD68+ 的小胶质细胞携带更多绝对 TSPO 并比 CD68− 小胶质细胞更大，但其细胞体积中 TSPO 的比例并未增加。由此可见，FTD 中升高的 TSPO–PET 信号很可能反映 CD68+ 吞噬性小胶质细胞负荷增加，而非其他细胞类型的 TSPO 表达，支持 TSPO–PET 作为跨 FTLD‑tau 与 FTLD‑TDP 的小胶质细胞负荷生物标志物。
